steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I touch it, one thing worth flagging: `/admin/reports` is the only route returning actual revenue data, and `app.listen` binds all interfaces — so "internal" here is a network assumption, not something the code enforces. Dropping `requireLogin` makes that endpoint readable by anything that can reach the port.

That's a one-line change either way, so the choice is yours:

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin but let it also accept a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token matched against an env var). The dashboard script sends the header; browsers keep using the session cookie. Still roughly one line in auth.js, and the route stays closed to unauthenticated callers.

options.label: Drop requireLogin
options.description: Remove the middleware from the route exactly as asked. /admin/reports becomes publicly readable to anyone who can reach the port, including the revenue rows. Simplest, and fine if something upstream (firewall, service mesh, bind address) already blocks outside traffic.

options.label: Separate unauthenticated route
options.description: Leave /admin/reports protected and add a new open route for the dashboard that serves only the fields the script needs. More code, but the admin boundary stays intact and the exposure is scoped to the data you intend to share.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

Changes in `server.js`:
- Removed `requireLogin` from the route (`server.js:7`).
- Dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open, so nobody later reads the missing middleware as an oversight and nobody assumes the endpoint is protected.

Left alone: `auth.js` still exports `requireLogin`. Nothing imports it now, but deleting it is a separate call and you may want it for the next admin route.

Verified: `node --check server.js` passes. No tests exist in the repo, so none were run — I did not start the server or hit the endpoint.

One loose end for whoever owns deployment: the protection for those revenue rows now lives entirely outside this repo, in whatever restricts reachability to the port. Worth confirming that's actually in place rather than assumed.
